description: Stored exposure equals the number of days in the period (values up to 365.0) for 114 training rows across the three policy tables (motor 47, buildings 33, contents 34); stored/date-derived ratio clusters at x365. Stored exposure for these rows summed to 35,703 against a true 97.8 exposure-years, i.e. they inflated total training exposure by 37% (motor 54,429 stored vs 38,969 derived).
action_detail: Exposure recomputed for EVERY policy and test row as (period_end - period_start + 1 day) / 365, rounded to 4 dp, which is the convention 99.5% of rows already follow (a 365-day row has exposure 1.0000; 1-day rows 0.0027). Rows in this cluster are flagged dq_exposure_class = 'day_count'. The same recomputation was run on the test files, where it is the identity (no test row deviates).
rationale: R-0001/R-0014: a ratio cluster at ~365 is a day count written into an exposure field. Date-derived exposure is the only trustworthy basis and is applied uniformly to training and test.

description: A second, smaller convention inside the 'looks fine' range: 495 training rows (motor 207, buildings 122, contents 166) carry exposure = days / 360 (stored/derived ratio 1.0139 = 365/360), visible only as a spike in the ratio tabulation after the day-count cluster is removed. Effect is small (+1.4% on those rows, +0.3 exposure-years in total) but it is a different basis.
action_detail: Repaired by the same date-based recomputation as F-01; flagged dq_exposure_class = 'basis_360'. Residual stored/derived ratio after removing both clusters lies within 4-dp rounding (0.986-1.004, all on rows shorter than 60 days).
rationale: R-0014 (amended): re-tabulate the residual after the obvious cluster; a 360-day basis sits at 1.014 and is a convention error, not rounding.

description: Negative result: the three test files carry no exposure defect. Stored exposure equals the inclusive-day/365 convention for all 209,063 test rows (max deviation 0.0001, rounding); no day-count or 360-day cluster. Test rows are clipped at 2025-12-31, so most are shorter than a year (mean exposure 0.87-0.91).
action_detail: Recomputation from dates applied anyway (identity); dq_exposure_class = 'ok' on every test row.
rationale: R-0014 requires the tabulation to be run on the test files separately because they can come from a different system; here they are clean and the audit trail records it.

description: Buildings sum_insured is x1,000 for 53 training rows and 104 test rows (values 60M-568M against a normal maximum of 894k). log10(sum_insured / written_premium) has its normal mass at 1.8-3.35 and the cluster at 4.96-6.2; the interval 3.35-4.96 is empty. Premium is unaffected (premium per 1,000 CU of SI is 1.03 for normal rows and 0.001 for the cluster), and other rows of the same policies carry the normal value (e.g. 238,000,000 in 2023 vs 245,000 in 2024).
action_detail: sum_insured divided by 1,000 where log10(sum_insured / written_premium) > 4.0 (boundary placed inside the empty interval); flagged dq_sum_insured_rescaled. Repaired values fall at 60,000-568,000, inside the normal range. Same rule and boundary applied to train, test and reference tables.
rationale: R-0003/R-0013: mass at a power of ten in a proportionality ratio is a unit error, not a large risk; the per-row ratio rule avoids a value threshold that would misclassify genuinely large houses. Same defect exists in the developed data (Part 1 treatment carries over).

description: Contents sum_insured is x1,000 for 57 training rows and 135 test rows (7.6M-131.6M against a normal maximum of 283k). log10(SI / premium): normal mass 2.0-2.8, cluster 5.16-5.7, empty interval 2.8-5.16.
action_detail: Same rule as F-04 (log-ratio > 4.0 -> divide by 1,000), flagged dq_sum_insured_rescaled; repaired values 7,600-131,600.

description: Negative result: no power-of-ten cluster in claim amounts (incurred / line-peril median is smooth from 10^-3.7 to 10^1.4 with no spike), in motor written_premium, in excesses, or in paid/incurred ratios (paid <= incurred for every claim; closed claims have paid == incurred; recoveries <= incurred).
action_detail: No change.
rationale: R-0003 requires every monetary column to be tabulated; the negative result is part of the audit trail.

description: Negative result: no claim repeats another on (policy_id, peril, loss_date, paid, incurred, recoveries) under a different claim_id; claim_id is unique; only 2 claims share policy and loss date (different perils, plausible).
action_detail: No change.
rationale: R-0002 content-key uniqueness check.

description: 36 claims (motor 28, buildings 3, contents 5; net incurred 92,267 = 0.33% of total) have a loss_date before the first period row of their policy (loss dates 2021-10-27 to 2023-07-04; 34 of them before the market's first policy row on 2023-01-01). All other 9,222 claims link to exactly one policy row by loss date (99.6% match, no multi-match, no claim on an unknown policy). Their report lags are 411-565 days, beyond the 99th percentile of the matched distribution for every peril involved (own damage 49 d, third-party property 90 d, glass 31 d, theft 25 d, storm 43 d, escape of water 87 d, flood 44 d); only bodily injury has such lags and one BI claim is among them but its loss date precedes any policy.
action_detail: Excluded from the cleaned claims table and from every target. Not re-dated. Share of incurred stated so the level effect is bounded (0.33% overall; 0.4% motor, 0.2% buildings, 0.4% contents).
rationale: R-0004: a loss date before the policy's first row is a date or linkage defect. R-0015: lags beyond the matched distribution's extreme quantile mark a date defect, not a late report; exclude and query rather than re-date.

description: Latest loss_date 2024-12-29 and latest report_date 2024-12-30 are consistent with the stated valuation date 2024-12-31; no claim falls in the 2025 test period. December 2024 has 263 reported claims against a Jan-Nov 2024 monthly mean of 388 (-32%), and November 330: the last calendar months are under-reported as expected. 20% of 2024 claims (38% of 2024 motor cost, 35% buildings, 18% contents) are open.
action_detail: No change to data. Carried into target construction: the cost-weighted completion curve gives 2024 full-year rows completion 0.80 (motor), 0.94 (buildings), 0.97 (contents).
rationale: R-0007 valuation-date check; R-0106 the last month's under-reporting must be carried by the completion curve, not an ad-hoc fix.

description: Policy year 2023 is a survivor sample: 100% of 2023 policies appear in 2024 (motor 20,084/20,084; buildings and contents likewise), and 2023 has no 'lapsed_by_customer' or 'cancelled' decisions at all, while 2024 shows 15% lapse/cancellation. The extract only reaches back to policies still in force in 2024. The developed data shows the same pattern in its first year (2021).
action_detail: Flagged dq_survivor_year in the modelling tables; labelled in the shift report and validation design (the 2023->2024 fold trains on survivors; 2023 frequency and mix are conditioned on survival).
rationale: R-0020 persistence audit.

description: 27 claims each exceed 2% of their line-accident-year net incurred: buildings fire claims dominate (10 of 12 in 2023 buildings; the largest single 2024 buildings claim, a fire of 361k, is 9.7% of that year), contents flood (9 claims at 2-4%), and one 2024 motor bodily-injury claim of 156k (2.0%). 2023 buildings carries 49 fire claims against 21 in 2024; the two years' buildings burning cost differs by 37% because of it.
action_detail: Not deleted. Handed to target construction: row targets capped at the 99th percentile of positive targets per line (motor 21,148; buildings 143,434; contents 19,968) and the excess given back as a line multiplier (1.078 / 1.119 / 1.053). Flagged dq_row_has_capped_loss. Mentioned wherever year-on-year or market comparisons are made.
rationale: R-0008: one such claim distorts trend, development and segment comparisons.

description: customer_service_contacts is an in-period count that grows mechanically with the claims it would predict: rows with 0 contacts have a 0.01% claim rate, 2 contacts 39%, 4+ contacts 94%; mean contacts rise from 0.4 (no claim) to 3.0 (one claim) to 8.1 (three). Its upper tail (up to 20) exists only in training; the test maximum is 5-6.
action_detail: Column kept in the cleaned tables (schema parity) but excluded from every feature set; carried in the modelling tables as x_customer_service_contacts.
rationale: R-0005 training-only tails in behavioural counts. missed_payments_12m and days_quote_to_inception were tested the same way and kept: same range in train and test, weak relation to claims.

description: campaign_code is null for exactly the 27,433 customers with customer_since_year <= 2022 and populated for every customer who joined in 2023-2025: its nullness is a deterministic function of join year (single-feature adversarial AUC 0.79 for 2024-train vs 2025-test).
action_detail: Excluded from features (x_campaign_code in the modelling tables). The code values themselves are uniformly distributed across campaigns within each cohort and carry no risk information.
rationale: R-0016 cohort-stamp detection: an attribute null exactly for customers who joined before a campaign existed is a time stamp.

description: customer_since_year is a join-year stamp (AUC 0.88 alone; every 2025 new customer has 2025) and is exactly reproduced by renewal_count: renewal_count = policy year - customer_since_year for all 318,359 rows. renewal_count is therefore the tenure form with the same meaning in every year (0 = new business).
action_detail: customer_since_year excluded from features (x_customer_since_year); renewal_count and new_business kept as mix features (R-0019): they shift because the portfolio changed (76% new business in 2025), not because their meaning changed.
rationale: R-0016/R-0019/R-0006: a join year is a time stamp; its relative form (tenure) is a risk factor.

description: occupation has 81 distinct raw values against a 20-value code list (plus null): case variants ('Retired', 'retired'), a trailing-space variant ('Retired '), and a 'Self-employed ' prefix attached to every base occupation including meaningless ones ('Self-employed retired', 'Self-employed student', 'Self-employed unemployed'). The variant shares are uniform across bases (Title 56%, 'Title ' 17%, lower 27%; prefix ~10% of each base), i.e. random corruption, not an attribute.
action_detail: Trimmed, case-folded, prefix stripped, re-cased to the developed-market code list (21 values incl. null); 59,899 values changed, 11,975 prefixes stripped. Flagged dq_occupation_normalised. Applies to test rows through the shared customers table.
rationale: R-0021 free-text noise test: uniform rate of a prefix across categories where it is meaningless marks random corruption to strip.

description: About 12% of values are null in: policies (motor vehicle_age, engine_size_cc, overnight_parking; buildings days_unoccupied, smoke_alarms; contents security_level, high_value_items), customers (occupation, marital_status, household_size, years_at_address) and addresses (distance_to_river_km, soil_type, roof_type, energy_rating; flood_zone 3%). Nulls are independent across columns (co-occurrence equals the product of rates), at the same rate in 2023, 2024, test, new business and renewals, and claim frequency of null vs non-null rows differs by less than noise on repaired exposure. The developed market has 2.5% in the same columns.
action_detail: No imputation. Nulls kept as their own 'unknown' level (native missing handling in the tree learner); no indicator features added because the nulls look like independent draws.
rationale: R-0018: test MAR before choosing a treatment; MCAR -> no indicator, no imputation to the mode.

description: expenses.commission_comparison_site is null for the emerging market while 5% of policies (and 5% of test rows) are written through comparison_site; all other channels, products and loadings are present (fixed expense 85 CU vs 45 developed, variable 15%, broker commission 20%, premium tax 8%, cat reinsurance 12% of property risk premium, profit margin 8%).
action_detail: Left null; not filled in. Raised as a premium-build question (missing loading or mislabelled channel).
rationale: R-0412: a missing entry in an expense or commission table is a premium-build question, never something to fill silently.

description: renewal_decision = 'declined_by_insurer' does not behave as a termination: all 181 policies declined in 2023 appear in 2024 and 167 of 181 declined in 2024 appear in the 2025 test rows (while 0 of 8,574 lapsed/cancelled 2024 policies do). The label is inconsistent with observed persistence.
action_detail: Kept as delivered; renewal_decision is excluded from features anyway (end-of-period information). Rows following a declined decision show higher frequency (motor 0.28 vs 0.17) but are too few to act on.
rationale: Found during the persistence audit; a human should confirm what the label means in this system.

description: Full-year 2024 rows run 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-30 (365 days inclusive in a leap year), leaving 2024-12-31 uncovered by any training row; 2023 and 2025 full-year rows end on 31 December. No claim has a loss date of 2024-12-31, so no linkage is affected.
action_detail: No change; noted so that a future extract with a claim on that day is not silently unlinked.
rationale: Found while reconciling the exposure convention (fixed 365-day rows rather than calendar years).

description: 120 claims have status 'repudiated' with paid, incurred and recoveries all 0.00.
action_detail: Kept in the cleaned claims table; contribute zero to every target and are excluded from claim counts and frequencies.
rationale: R-0101: repudiated claims contribute zero; keeping them preserves the audit trail.

description: New business is 14-15% of training rows but 76% of test rows (158,980 rows). None of the 2025 new-business policy_ids appears in training (the acquired broker book), while every 2025 renewal row's policy exists in 2024. The training new-business segment is small (motor 6,535 rows / 697 claims; buildings 3,786 / 77; contents 4,716 / 102) but matches the test book on age mix (both skew to 17-34 and 65+) and channel (70% broker, 25% direct, 5% comparison site). Age-standardised, training new business runs at 1.18x renewal frequency and 1.43x cost in motor, 1.29x/1.23x in contents, and 0.93x/0.82x in buildings (thin).
action_detail: Kept; new_business and renewal_count retained as features (mix, R-0019). The model's new-business relativity is compared with these pre-model figures in validation; models are scored on the new-business subset (R-0406).
rationale: R-0407/R-0410 acquired-portfolio check.

description: The weather table carries 2025 values for every address; 2025 differs systematically from 2023-24 (rainfall 1,251 vs 1,378 mm, freezing days 29 vs 17-21, hail days 11 vs 14-17, temperature 14.2 vs 15.3-15.8), so every weather column separates 2024 from 2025 alone (AUC 0.68-0.77; PSI 0.45-0.96 on renewal rows where nothing else changed). Weather is a calendar-year stamp here, not a risk factor that transfers.
action_detail: Excluded from the baseline feature set (x_ columns in the modelling tables); re-adding it as a group is a registered test (R-0302). Address-level climate differences between markets (hail, wildfire, freezing) are described in the shift report.
rationale: R-0006 adversarial validation; R-0302 Part 1 found weather hurt out-of-year performance.

description: reference_policies (20 rows: 7 motor, 7 buildings, 6 contents) are all 2025 test rows present in the test files with identical row_ids and policy_ids; exposure matches the date convention exactly and log10(SI/premium) is at most 3.18 (no unit error). Column types differ from the line tables (years_licensed, ncb_years, seats as double) because the wide table holds nulls for other lines' columns.
action_detail: Copied through unchanged.
rationale: R-0013 requires the same unit rule on reference tables; recorded as a negative result.

description: vehicle_age has no value below 3 in the emerging market (train and test; 3-27) whereas the developed market runs 0-28 with a median of 7 vs 10 here. Either the market has no new-vehicle business or vehicle_age is defined differently (e.g. years since first registration abroad).
action_detail: Kept as delivered and used as a feature (same support in train and test). Mapping note added to schema_mapping.md; a human should confirm the definition before any developed-market relativity for vehicle age is borrowed.
rationale: Found in the schema/shift comparison (R-0401/R-0402).

description: 60 training rows and 71 test rows have period_start == period_end (exposure 0.0027 = 1/365); in training most are 'mid_term_change' rows dated 1 January, i.e. a change effective on renewal day that the system records as a one-day row before the new row starts.
action_detail: Kept; consistent with the inclusive-day convention and with the following row starting the next day. They carry negligible exposure and no claims.
rationale: Observation from the period-structure profiling.
